description: YuNet face detector from OpenCV Zoo. THE SELECTED DETECTOR: chosen over SCRFD because its weights are permissively licensed, and issue #3 leaves SCRFD's pretrained weights unusable for anything but development.

license.training_data: WIDER FACE. Its terms are separate from the model's and need their own check.
license.note: Desk assessment: OpenCV Zoo publishes YuNet under MIT for both code and weights, which is why it is the selected detector rather than SCRFD. NOT VERIFIED at source -- a human must read the current licence and set verified/verified_at before this can be promoted past candidate.

eval.note: No benchmark has been run. YuNet is expected to trail SCRFD on small faces, which is the case that matters in group photos. The cost lands as recall, not precision: a missed face is absent from an album, while the precision-first threshold and review queue keep a wrong face out. Quantifying the gap is the first eval-harness job.

notes:
SCORE RULE: confidence is sqrt(clamp(cls,0,1) * clamp(obj,0,1)) -- the clamped GEOMETRIC MEAN of the separate classification and objectness heads, which is why both appear in outputs. It is declared as the `geometric_mean_score` step so a registry-driven host can apply it without hardcoding anything per model id. An earlier version of this file said the product, and at score_threshold 0.6 the product discards roughly 84% of the detections YuNet accepts -- which reads as a weak detector rather than a bug. Confirmed against opencv/modules/objdetect/src/face_detect.cpp.

DECODER: not SCRFD's distance-to-four-sides. Boxes are centre-offset plus exponentiated size; landmarks are cell-relative and linear.

NMS: OpenCV rounds each box to an integer cv::Rect2i BEFORE cv::dnn::NMSBoxes, so IoU is computed on integer rectangles and its width/height convention differs from a float box by one pixel. Declared as `integer_rect_nms` rather than plain `nms` because the two disagree on boxes sitting near the IoU threshold -- and a disagreement there means one face becomes two, or two adjacent faces in a group photo become one.

THRESHOLDS: 0.6 and 0.3 are the OpenCV Zoo defaults, starting points rather than tuned values; re-tune against our own benchmark libraries before promotion.

COORDINATES: decoded against the letterboxed 640x640 input, and must be un-letterboxed before being normalised against the ORIENTED image for FaceRecord.

SHAPES AND BATCHING CORRECTED AGAINST THE REAL GRAPH. The declared output shapes were rank-2 [-1, C]; the checkpoint emits rank-3 [1, N, C] with N fixed per stride (6400/1600/400 at 640x640, matching 80x80/40x40/20x20 grids with one anchor per location -- unlike SCRFD's two). Batching claimed supported/max 8/dynamic; the graph's input is a static [1, 3, 640, 640], so batch is 1 and the input size is not negotiable either. execution.py clamps max_batch to the session's static batch dimension, so the wrong claim was survivable rather than harmless -- it was a description of the model that disagreed with the model.
